task6ab.review: Four Important findings addressed in independent scoped review

rulings.record: stop the owned 856-test broad regression run after 18 minutes at 8% with multiple prerequisite/legacy fixture failures; keep its log explicitly incomplete and unpassed, finish the two relevant export compatibility runs, and move comprehensive acceptance to Task 6 after all domain handlers exist — focused Task 2 coverage is complete, and repeating unrelated unavailable integration paths does not improve Task 2 evidence — cost if wrong: an unrelated regression may surface later at Task 6/final review rather than at this gate.

spatial assets attach immutable asset_id/artifact_version and spatial metadata to an existing authorized object's governed revision, reusing existing audit/authorization rather than creating a parallel resource-kind engine; GIS indexes independent asset history, and verified quality requires verified object nature plus authorized survey evidence — this matches the approved shared identity/current-permission model — cost if wrong: standalone assets that lack any semantic object would later need an explicit governed resource type. Governed location observations are distinct from Task 5 high-frequency tracks, which must not emit a full RDF revision per point; attachment/evidence authorization remains current on reads and writes.

waiting for an unapplied GIS dependency delays and releases an RDF job without exhausting its execution-failure budget; capped/terminal GIS delivery failure must remain explicitly observable as a blocked dependency, with existing delivery retry limits preserved — a recoverable store outage must not permanently consume unrelated semantic work retries — cost if wrong: longer-lived queued/blocked jobs require operator visibility and recovery controls. Task 3 adds focused pause/resume and unrelated-job progress coverage.

extend existing governed jobs retry for DOMAIN_DELIVERY_FAILED to reset only failed GIS delivery receipts required by the job's exact accepted event(s), retaining immutable envelope IDs, current authorization, If-Match/idempotency and audited previous failure/attempts — Task 1 lacks a governed capped-delivery recovery path, and manual owner SQL is inadequate as the normal outage recovery procedure — cost if wrong: a small cross-module dependency between job retry and synchronization must be maintained. Task 3 owns focused authorized/unauthorized/unrelated-delivery protection and actual recovery-to-Fuseki coverage, without new auth engine or UI.

preserve out-of-order immutable GIS history via an explicitly registered history/superseded callback, atomically with target inbox, after existing semantic conflict/order checks; leave generic/GIS current heads monotonic and default delivery behavior unchanged — repeating all historical geometry/assets/locations in each envelope would grow quadratically — cost if wrong: each specialized callback must uphold append-only and head invariants. Envelopes carry bounded per-event changes, original events supply old history; history queries must expose still-pending/failed accepted events. Task 3 adds callback rollback/replay/order tests and scoped Task 1 delivery regression. Tasks 4/5 must consider this optional interface when preserving out-of-order catalog or observation history.

use a governed operator-controlled stopped-writer maintenance window and durable checked activation artifact, keeping core identity in place for legacy GIS/blob migration; do not add live routing or claim checkbox-only quiescence. Split remaining Task 6 into 6A migration/compatible rollback, 6B coordinated whole-store restore, 6C integrated acceptance/docs. Legacy reads may activate only after all accepted versions are represented; incompatible split-only catalog/telemetry changes must refuse downgrade and use the 6B restore path — approved spec section 9 permits paused writers and recovery from a new backup, while static global legacy routing cannot safely represent new domains — cost if wrong: operations need downtime and a compatible recovery deployment instead of an instant old-config rollback; more automated routing would require later work. Task 6 remains incomplete until the full restore alternative is actually implemented/tested.

regroup 6A migration and 6B coordinated backup/restore into one 6AB implementation/review gate, retaining the same informed implementer and BASE 7a0a28b; keep 6C acceptance/docs separate — real activation cannot be accepted before its real backup/reference-completeness producer exists, and a synthetic self-reported receipt is not evidence — cost if wrong: this operational review becomes larger and its acceptance later, but no partial migration is represented as safely complete. This supersedes only the separate 6A-before-6B sequencing, not the stopped-writer or preservation requirements.

keep 6AB focused by rejecting nonrepresentable legacy semantic-object heads during migration, while carrying the confirmed direct-attachment/object-revision mismatch as an OPEN integration correctness item for 6C/final gating — direct ArtifactService.register_upload can advance resource_heads with evidence.attached without advancing semantic_objects or producing a GIS delivery; changing the backup fixture owner does not verify that normal object path — cost if wrong: affected legacy objects require explicit repair and the later integration task may need a scoped artifact/semantic revision fix. Do not silently accept this as a permanent operating limitation or mark overall work complete without disposition. Implementer must preserve a focused reproducer and public-route/baseline trace in task-6ab-report.md.

repair evidenced legacy semantic-object attachment/head divergence through a narrow append-only authenticated evidence reconciliation command, requiring exact current If-Match, a contiguous recognized legacy evidence.attached tail and current authority over every retained dependency; preserve all old revisions, record exact repair inputs, and require the new exact GIS delivery before split current reads — the approved migration/history requirements need a real recovery path without rewriting immutable evidence, and ordinary attachment handling can reuse the existing governed record_state path — cost if wrong: one small maintenance API and its authorization/version invariants require ongoing support; unknown intervening states remain refused rather than silently reconstructed. Snapshot selection must preserve geometry removal/withdrawal and cannot generally skip an unknown newer state to resurrect history.

catalog terminal-delivery retry uses a separately scoped catalog.delivery_retry audit resource, exact original accepted reference/event and unchanged payload/version, with current catalog.manage/dependency authority, current baseline, existing idempotency and atomic audit/reset; it does not manufacture a new catalog metadata head — standalone exhausted catalog events must be recoverable without repeating the known generic-head divergence, and failed semantic-job retry alone cannot cover them — cost if wrong: the small operational audit resource needs its own correctly linked current-authorization and retention behavior; future domain retries must preserve this distinction. Pending/acknowledged/unrelated events are not reset. Named catalog release receipt risk is now confirmed by implementer code inspection and awaits RED/GREEN pending/failed/lost-ack/applied evidence.

the new owned Fuseki lifecycle refuses to adopt or stop a running legacy PID marker without its recorded process incarnation; an explicitly stopped, verified owned state may enter the documented upgrade/start path while retaining its configuration and TDB data — PID reuse cannot prove ownership, and fresh/stopped public reproduction must not sacrifice the retained-runtime boundary — cost if wrong: legacy running installations need a one-time operator-verified stop and maintenance transition before the new runner can manage them; no automatic in-place adoption. Retained23030 remains untouched during this fix. Validate stopped-state identity/config/free-port and record the new incarnation; never fabricate a PID marker or erase source data.

implement the controlled archive interface required by authoritative spec6.2 despite the narrower preview-only implementation-plan wording, as an authorized auditable bounded immutable record archive that retains all source rows, accepted versions and evidence; do not delete/detach data, invent retention durations or claim cold-storage tiering — missing business retention values do not prevent a safe non-destructive archival contract — cost if wrong: archives consume additional storage and operators must manage explicit bounded selections; physical space reclamation and automatic lifecycle policies remain future work rather than an assumed effect of archiving.

original_cannot_verify_items: Actual Compose startup, images/network/mount behavior and container persistence: there is no Docker engine in the supplied environment; configuration validation is not execution.

Physically disconnected deployment or full OS/container egress enforcement: the Python socket guard does not sandbox native libpq or service processes. Browser operation under genuinely disconnected target networking remains unexecuted.

Production throughput, latency, timeout suitability, camera counts or retention capacity: graph/SPARQL failed the saved workload, production worker defaults remain unqualified, and hardware/workload/measurement limitations above apply.

Full original P0+P1 completion or a green full 856-case suite: neither is established by this branch. Earlier frontend visual work remains paused. Historic focused checks do not combine into a fresh whole-product pass.

Live camera/NVR/ONVIF/vendor-cloud/drone protocols, actual firmware capabilities, real source CDC guarantees, or field-device control: the implemented adapters and samples are generic/synthetic, and remote control is expressly excluded.

Real field identity, surveyed horizontal/vertical accuracy, actual farm/pond/orchard boundaries, installed counts, real image/video quality and professional truth promotion: required source material and accountable verification have not been supplied.

Production migration, production cutover, operational RPO/RTO, OIDC/enterprise disaster recovery, host power-loss durability, HA/failover, or independent administrator fencing: isolated native platform-data restoration and stopped-writer assumptions do not prove these.

Every S3/AWS feature, object lock, garbage collection, physical storage quota, arbitrary multipart object size or hostile external S3 writer behavior: only the supported and exercised private provider paths are evidenced.

New end-to-end recovery of GIS asset/location records for I1/I2, or actual-store outage behavior for I3 after a fix: the reviewer probes demonstrate defects but are deliberately service-free. Scoped follow-through remains required.

Fresh final-head TypeScript/build/test acceptance or behavior of a future fix commit: no such checks were rerun during this review. Existing recorded checks are evidence only for their stated revisions and scopes.

Third-party per-file reuse rights, correctness of every external publication or live reference URL: public sources/pins and acknowledged rights limitations were reviewed as project evidence; no new external legal/content verification was performed.

verification_disposition.1-8: Remain explicit environment/field/production limits; not claimed passed or fulfilled by mocks.
verification_disposition.9: Focused affected GIS backup/restore/read evidence is preserved in the fix acceptance record; injected boundary tests are distinguished from actual native store checks.
verification_disposition.10: Changed contracts receive actual OpenAPI/TypeScript/build and covering test execution in the fix evidence, not a repeated full-product matrix or new benchmark.
verification_disposition.11: Only fixed previously inspected primary sources and original fixtures are used; no new third-party code reuse or legal conclusion is claimed.

considered_behaviors_acknowledged_by_con: Full live device integrations, remote actuator control, new 3D reconstruction/visual frontend, OCR/vector search and mandatory LLM extraction: expressly excluded or postponed by the approved scope; generic contracts still must meet I4/I5.
Real field values, surveyed geometry, device count, encoding/bitrate values and retention durations: no reliable field inputs exist. Nullable structures are appropriate; invented data would be wrong.
Docker/physical-offline acceptance: unavailable environment is an explicit recorded boundary, not a reason to label configuration as passed or to modify host virtualization during review.

Further graph/SPARQL engine redesign or another benchmark run: actual failures are conspicuous and performance remains unqualified; no new speculative optimization was authorized by the review. M4 narrows what the existing domain-view samples establish.

Changing production worker defaults solely to match 240/300: the native profile is workload evidence, not a demonstrated universal production setting. No basis to select production capacity values here.

S3 Range materializing/verifying a whole object before slicing: documented correctness-first behavior; potentially expensive for large media but not a newly hidden regression. Physical capacity and resumable-part/orphan GC remain disclosed operational work, not a fabricated completed feature.

Huge single-object S3 limits, sustained worker queue fairness, and historical location validity beyond exact pins: plausible scale/semantics risks were considered, but this pass did not establish a concrete violated supported case. They remain unverified; I am not asserting them as bugs from speculation.

Shared PostgreSQL failure domain and stopped-writer/direct-admin trust boundary: explicit approved architecture and operations assumptions. They must not be advertised as independent HA or distributed fencing.

Catalog/telemetry split-only rollback refusal: correct fail-closed behavior when legacy cannot represent post-cutover writes; separately verified isolated compatible restore is the recovery path. Refusal alone remains insufficient recovery evidence.

Legacy attachment-history repair and terminal catalog retry behavior: final code and accepted focused evidence address the named earlier defects; no reason was found to reopen those findings merely because prior versions failed.

Current authorization hiding unavailable-to-the-user evidence: deliberate non-disclosure remains valid. I3 concerns suppressing operational errors for otherwise authorized assets, not removal of hidden-row filtering.

Model/device lifecycle placement and semantic assertions versus fixed catalog columns: physical device lifecycle can properly be semantic data and must not be confused with model identity. I5 asks for a demonstrated structured mapping of explicit metadata requirements, not one prescribed SQL table layout.

Existing RDFLib deprecation warnings and compact/minified Python style: warnings and maintainability costs are real but no new user-facing failure was established. No pristine-output claim or broad formatting rewrite is warranted in this fix wave.

Retained test/orphan domain rows and partition-parent/child count overlap: documented fixture/inventory facts, not accepted business totals. I2 is specifically missing accepted effects, not a demand to purge unrelated negative evidence.

Word rerendering for metadata-only hash correction: the binary is already checked and M2 changes provenance scope, not layout. Content changes for final dispositions may require normal scoped render QA; a metadata correction alone does not.
Remote push/merge and public publication actions: outside the reviewer role. The user-authorized controller owns integration after findings are resolved; this review performs no remote mutation.
whole_branch_review.scope_statement: All considered and declined-to-judge behaviors were acknowledged. There is no assertion of full original P0+P1, production/standard-hardware performance, Docker/physical-offline qualification or actual field truth.

benchmark_visibility.boundary: Measured identities had view/edit but no source.read; domain views did not return seeded observations/media. Setup used a different authorized actor. These latencies do not qualify populated professional data reads.
benchmark_visibility.future_driver: Intended source/evidence rights and expected professional record identities must be checked before timing. The scoped fixture check is not a repeated baseline benchmark.
